verdict.line: You lose if Jayce solo-kills you in a Hammer-stance all-in or Cannon-stance poke before level 6; you win if you survive to Cannibalism and grind him down, which is why Sion sits at 54.6% over 194 games despite the lane itself grading even.

brief.thesis: Sion has zero ranged answer to Jayce's two stances, so OP.GG's own tip holds: before level 3 you must give ground and let him poke rather than trade. Once your kit and Grasp sustain come online, the matchup inverts hard, because Jayce has no tool that out-heals Cannibalism's leech or outlasts a champion whose max HP grows every time he kills something with Enrage.

theirWindow.what: He's kiting with Shock Blast (600 range) and using Acceleration Gate to speed up his own pokes. You have no gap closer at this point, so don't chase — just last-hit, eat the chip damage, and wait for your Doran's Shield regen to cover it.

yourWindow.when: Jayce just leapt in on Hammer Q (To the Skies!)
yourWindow.what: His only engage/disengage tool is now down for 16 to 8 seconds depending on rank. Pop W (Death's Caress) for the shield, turn on E, and Q (Cryptic Gaze) to stun him in place — he can't bail until his R flips him back to Cannon on its own 6s cooldown, and even then he still has no leap.

powerCurve.note: No ranged answer to his early pokes
Q stun online, trades start to even out
Tank items wear down his sustained poke

start.why: Its regen directly covers the chip damage from Jayce's Cannon-stance poke, letting you follow OP.GG's plan of keeping distance and slowly gaining control instead of forcing early trades.

boots.why: Both his Hammer-stance empowered autos and his basic attacks are physical, so flat armor reduces every poke source he has, not just one.

core.why: The burn punishes him for ever standing in melee range when his R forces him into Hammer stance, and the HP pool pairs with Enrage's health-spending AD.
The shield-and-heal proc answers his exact poke-then-reset pattern by giving you sustain back the moment he disengages in Cannon stance.
His whole kit is sustained physical autos — empowered Hammer hits plus basic attacks — so Thornmail punishes every single one he lands on you.

situational.when: he's adding magic damage sources late and you want flat resist scaling on top of your other tank items
you're already ahead and want to add wave clear and poke damage on top of your tank stats
the game is going long and you want raw HP scaling instead of Thornmail's attack-based punish

runes.keystoneWhy: It heals you and grants bonus max HP every time you land an auto on him, which directly counters the poke-and-reset rhythm Jayce plays in both stances — every trade you land sustains you back up.

summoners.why: Flash answers his Hammer-stance knockback and leap all-ins, while Teleport lets you reset after losing an early poke exchange and still catch your level-6 and item power spikes on time — the dominant pick at 56% win rate and 85.8% pick rate for this matchup.

playing.title: Hold trades until level 3
playing.detail: Before level 3 you don't have the stun rank or shield strength to win a Hammer-stance exchange, so last-hit and absorb Cannon-stance poke rather than forcing anything.

playing.title: Punish his stance swaps
playing.detail: His R (6s cooldown) is what switches Hammer and Cannon — if he swaps mid-fight to disengage into Cannon, only chase if your E is already on, or you'll just eat another Shock Blast.

playing.title: W before every commitment
playing.detail: Pop Death's Caress the instant he commits to a Hammer-stance auto or Q leap; the shield absorbs his burst and still detonates on him afterward.

playing.title: Toggle E only after Q lands
playing.detail: Enrage costs health per attack, so only turn it on right after your stun connects — whiffing it just bleeds HP for nothing.

playing.title: Survive to level 6, then all-in
playing.detail: Cannibalism is your lane-winning tool — once it's up, force fights in melee range where his knockback and Lightning Field tick can't out-damage your leech.

playing.title: Scale through his poke
playing.detail: Sunfire Aegis and Unending Despair's healing let you walk down his Cannon-stance kiting by level 11 to 13 — out-scale him rather than trying to out-trade him.

playing.title: Respect his R first-hit
playing.detail: The first attack after he transforms (either stance) carries a bonus — armor shred or extra magic damage — so if you're missing Q, back off instead of soaking that hit.

brief.patchCaveat: The build, runes, and win rates above come from measured current-patch games (194 Sion-vs-Jayce top games); the stance-tracking and timing advice is my own read of the mechanics.

stats.opponentTip: Avoid being punished by Jayce before reaching level 3 by keeping your distance. Use your skills to poke to slowly gain control over lane.
